lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: checking a total before trusting it
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: checking a total before trusting it

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: A school raised $3,200 in September and $2,750 in October, then spent $1,400 on new books. How much remains?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A charity collected $13352 in the spring and $4761 in the fall, then spent $2827 on supplies. How much money remains?
A charity collected $86330 in the spring and $35789 in the fall, then spent $16044 on supplies. How much money remains?
A charity collected $41571 in the spring and $21395 in the fall, then received an extra $4389 donation. How much money is there in total?
A charity collected $66278 in the spring and $12166 in the fall, then spent $7814 on supplies. How much money remains?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A charity collected $38103 in the spring and $37308 in the fall, then spent $9146 on supplies. How much money remains?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A charity collected $28868 in the spring and $22307 in the fall, then spent $6079 on supplies. How much money remains?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
